topic: What if you went back to 2010 with $100?

script.text: So, what do you buy? Not toys. Not trainers. You buy the strangest thing in 2010. Bitcoin.

Right now almost nobody has heard of it. It's a nerdy experiment on a forum. A coin is worth less than a penny. On the twenty-second of May, a man in Florida pays ten thousand bitcoins for two pizzas. That's real.
So you find someone on the forum, and you send them your hundred dollars. They send you ten thousand coins. The same pile that just bought two pizzas. They think you're an idiot. You let them.
Then you wait. You can't tell anyone. You can't touch it. You just check the price, every single night, under the covers. And while you wait, you have a little fun.

Your best friend Mo is obsessed with the World Cup. You tell him Spain will win the final. One–nil. A goal from Iniesta, in extra time, in the one hundred and sixteenth minute. Mo laughs at you. Then on the eleventh of July, the ball hits the net in the one hundred and sixteenth minute. Mo stares at you like you're a ghost. 'Do it again.'

So you do. You tell him a photo app called Instagram is coming in October. It comes in October. You tell him about a block game called Minecraft that everyone will be playing. He thinks it looks terrible. Now he's building a castle every night.
Then, in February 2011, it happens. One bitcoin is worth one dollar. Your hundred dollars just became ten thousand.
In early June, it hits thirty-one dollars. Your hundred dollars is now worth three hundred and ten thousand. You're a kid, and you're secretly richer than everyone on your street.
But here's the thing about magic internet money. It can disappear just as fast.

science.claim: On 22 May 2010, Laszlo Hanyecz paid 10,000 BTC for two pizzas, the first known real-world bitcoin purchase.
science.working: Laszlo Hanyecz of Jacksonville, Florida, offered 10,000 BTC on the BitcoinTalk forum for two pizzas; the trade happened on 22 May 2010 (about $41 at the time).
science.source: Bitcoin Pizza Day; BitcoinTalk forum thread 'Pizza for bitcoins?' (2010)

science.claim: Spain beat the Netherlands 1–0 in the 2010 World Cup final; Andrés Iniesta scored in the 116th minute.
science.working: Spain beat the Netherlands 1-0 after extra time in Johannesburg on 11 July 2010; Iniesta scored in the 116th minute.
science.source: FIFA, 2010 World Cup final match report (11 July 2010)

science.claim: Instagram launched on the App Store on 6 October 2010.
science.working: Instagram was released on the iOS App Store on 6 October 2010.

science.claim: Bitcoin first reached $1 on 9 February 2011 and about $31 in June 2011 on Mt. Gox.
science.working: Bitcoin reached parity with the US dollar on Mt. Gox on 9 February 2011 and peaked near $31.9 on 8 June 2011. 10,000 BTC x $31 = $310,000.
science.source: Mt. Gox price history; CoinDesk, Bitcoin price history
